items.q: The assessable profit of a company is N3000000 and a balancing charge of N200000 arises on the disposal of an asset. What is the total profit?
items.s: Total profit = assessable profit + balancing charge = 3000000 + 200000 = 3200000 naira.

items.q: A chargeable asset was acquired for N7000000 and later sold for N12000000. Incidental costs of N450000 were incurred on the sale. What is the chargeable gain?
items.s: Chargeable gain = proceeds - acquisition cost - incidental costs = 12000000 - 7000000 - 450000 = 4550000 naira.

items.q: A chargeable gain of N2000000 arises and capital gains tax is charged at 10 percent. What is the tax payable?
A taxable supply is made for N400000 before tax and value added tax is charged at 7.5 percent. What tax is added?
A company declares a dividend of N1600000 to its shareholders and withholds tax at 10 percent. What tax is withheld?
items.s: Tax withheld = dividend x 10/100 = 1600000 x 10/100 = 160000 naira.

items.q: An assessment of N2400000 has been raised and the taxpayer has already paid N2000000 against it. What balance is still outstanding?
items.s: Balance = assessment - amount paid = 2400000 - 2000000 = 400000 naira.

items.q: An employee earns gross income of N4200000 in a year. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200000 or 1 percent of gross income, plus 20 percent of gross income. What is the taxable income?
items.s: Relief = higher of N200000 and 1 percent of 4200000 = N200000; allowance = 200000 + 20 percent of 4200000 = 1040000; taxable income = 4200000 - 1040000 = 3160000 naira.

items.q: A taxpayer has gross income of N1800000. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200000 or 1 percent of gross income, plus 20 percent of gross income. What is the allowance?
items.s: The fixed part is the higher of N200000 and N18000, and the proportional part is 20 percent of 1800000 = N360000, so the allowance is 200000 + 360000 = 560000 naira.

items.q: An individual has taxable income of N1500000 and pays tax at 20 percent. What is the income left after tax?
Taxable income is N700000. The first N300000 is charged at 11 percent and the balance at 24 percent. What is the total tax?
An individual with taxable income of N3600000 paid tax of N480000. What is the average rate of tax as a percentage?
items.s: Average rate = total tax/taxable income x 100 = 480000/3600000 x 100 = 13.33 percent.

items.q: An employee earns basic salary of N4200000 a year and contributes 10 percent of it to a pension scheme. What amount is allowed as relief for the contribution?
items.s: Relief = basic salary x rate/100 = 4200000 x 10/100 = 420000 naira.

items.q: A company has total profit of N9000000 and pays company income tax at 30 percent. What is the tax charge?
items.s: Tax charge = total profit x rate/100 = 9000000 x 30/100 = 2700000 naira.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N8500000 and capital allowances of N1600000. What is the chargeable profit?
items.s: Chargeable profit = assessable profit - capital allowances = 8500000 - 1600000 = 6900000 naira.

items.q: A company made a profit of N5000000 for the year and has an unused loss of N2500000 brought forward from an earlier year. What profit is liable to tax?
items.s: Profit liable = profit for the year - loss brought forward = 5000000 - 2500000 = 2500000 naira.

items.q: A company has assessable profit of N12000000 and pays tertiary education tax at 2.5 percent. What is the charge?
items.s: Education tax = assessable profit x 2.5/100 = 12000000 x 2.5/100 = 300000 naira.

items.q: A company has a profit of N8000000 and its total tax charge for the year was N2400000. What is its effective tax rate as a percentage?
items.s: Effective rate = tax charge/profit x 100 = 2400000/8000000 x 100 = 30 percent.

items.q: A company bought plant costing N4500000 and is granted an initial allowance of 25 percent. What is the initial allowance?
items.s: Initial allowance = cost x rate/100 = 4500000 x 25/100 = 1125000 naira.

items.q: A qualifying asset cost N3000000. Initial allowance of 50 percent was granted in the first year and the annual allowance is 15 percent of the written down value. What is the annual allowance in the second year?
items.s: Written down value = 3000000 - 1500000 = 1500000; annual allowance = 1500000 x 15/100 = 225000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N900000 is sold for N1500000. What is the balancing charge?
items.s: Balancing charge = sale proceeds - written down value = 1500000 - 900000 = 600000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N1200000 is sold for N400000. What is the balancing allowance?
items.s: Balancing allowance = written down value - sale proceeds = 1200000 - 400000 = 800000 naira.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N5000000 and capital allowances of N3200000. Capital allowances may be claimed only up to two thirds of the assessable profit. What amount of capital allowance is allowed against the profit?
items.s: Two thirds of the assessable profit is 3333333; the allowance claimed is limited to the lower of that and 3200000, which is 3200000 naira.

items.q: An asset was sold for N10000000 and N500000 was paid out in fees connected with the sale. What are the net proceeds of disposal?
items.s: Net proceeds = gross proceeds - costs of disposal = 10000000 - 500000 = 9500000 naira.

items.q: A registered trader charged output tax of N1800000 for the month and suffered input tax of N900000. What value added tax is payable?
items.s: Tax payable = output tax - input tax = 1800000 - 900000 = 900000 naira.

items.q: A price of N860000 includes value added tax at 7.5 percent. What amount of the price is the tax?
items.s: Tax = inclusive price x 7.5/107.5 = 860000 x 7.5/107.5 = 60000 naira.

items.q: A taxable supply was invoiced at N1620000 inclusive of value added tax at 7.5 percent. What is the price before tax?
items.s: Price before tax = inclusive amount x 100/107.5 = 1620000 x 100/107.5 = 1506976 naira.

items.q: A company pays a supplier N5000000 for a contract and must withhold tax at 10 percent. How much tax is withheld?
items.s: Tax withheld = gross payment x rate/100 = 5000000 x 10/100 = 500000 naira.

items.q: A payment of N2400000 is subject to withholding tax at 5 percent. What amount reaches the payee?
A company pays N2000000 for professional services, taxed at 10 percent, and N500000 as rent, taxed at 5 percent. What total withholding tax must it remit?
A dividend of N6000000 is paid to a shareholder and tax of 10 percent is withheld as a final tax. What amount does the shareholder receive?
items.s: Tax withheld = 6000000 x 10/100 = 600000; amount received = 6000000 - 600000 = 5400000 naira.

items.q: A taxpayer files his return late and the law imposes a penalty equal to 10 percent of the tax due. The tax due is N3000000. What is the penalty?
items.s: Penalty = tax due x 10/100 = 3000000 x 10/100 = 300000 naira.

items.q: Tax of N2400000 is paid 6 months late and interest is charged at 2 percent for each month of delay. What interest is payable?
items.s: Interest = tax x rate/100 x months = 2400000 x 2/100 x 6 = 288000 naira.

items.q: A trader made sales of N4000000 during the month and collected value added tax of N500000. What is the tax as a percentage of sales?
items.s: Tax as a percentage of sales = 500000/4000000 x 100 = 12.5 percent.

items.q: The tax declared by a taxpayer was N2400000 but a tax audit established that N4000000 was properly due. What is the tax shortfall?
items.s: Shortfall = correct liability - amount declared = 4000000 - 2400000 = 1600000 naira.

items.q: An individual has taxable income of N3000000 and falls into the top band, which is charged at 24 percent. What is the tax on the whole income at that rate?
items.s: Tax = taxable income x rate/100 = 3000000 x 24/100 = 720000 naira.

items.q: Gross income for the year is N2600000 and the total reliefs allowed are N600000. What is the taxable income?
items.s: Taxable income = gross income - reliefs = 2600000 - 600000 = 2000000 naira.

items.q: The assessable profit of a company is N5600000 and a balancing charge of N350000 arises on the disposal of an asset. What is the total profit?
items.s: Total profit = assessable profit + balancing charge = 5600000 + 350000 = 5950000 naira.

items.q: A chargeable asset was acquired for N4000000 and later sold for N6000000. Incidental costs of N450000 were incurred on the sale. What is the chargeable gain?
items.s: Chargeable gain = proceeds - acquisition cost - incidental costs = 6000000 - 4000000 - 450000 = 1550000 naira.

items.q: A chargeable gain of N3500000 arises and capital gains tax is charged at 10 percent. What is the tax payable?
A taxable supply is made for N800000 before tax and value added tax is charged at 7.5 percent. What tax is added?
An assessment of N3200000 has been raised and the taxpayer has already paid N2600000 against it. What balance is still outstanding?
items.s: Balance = assessment - amount paid = 3200000 - 2600000 = 600000 naira.

items.q: An employee earns gross income of N3600000 in a year. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200000 or 1 percent of gross income, plus 20 percent of gross income. What is the taxable income?
items.s: Relief = higher of N200000 and 1 percent of 3600000 = N200000; allowance = 200000 + 20 percent of 3600000 = 920000; taxable income = 3600000 - 920000 = 2680000 naira.

items.q: A taxpayer has gross income of N3000000. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200000 or 1 percent of gross income, plus 20 percent of gross income. What is the allowance?
items.s: The fixed part is the higher of N200000 and N30000, and the proportional part is 20 percent of 3000000 = N600000, so the allowance is 200000 + 600000 = 800000 naira.

items.q: An individual has taxable income of N2000000 and pays tax at 20 percent. What is the income left after tax?
Taxable income is N700000. The first N500000 is charged at 15 percent and the balance at 21 percent. What is the total tax?
An individual with taxable income of N2400000 paid tax of N480000. What is the average rate of tax as a percentage?
items.s: Average rate = total tax/taxable income x 100 = 480000/2400000 x 100 = 20 percent.

items.q: An employee earns basic salary of N2400000 a year and contributes 8 percent of it to a pension scheme. What amount is allowed as relief for the contribution?
items.s: Relief = basic salary x rate/100 = 2400000 x 8/100 = 192000 naira.

items.q: A company has total profit of N2400000 and pays company income tax at 20 percent. What is the tax charge?
items.s: Tax charge = total profit x rate/100 = 2400000 x 20/100 = 480000 naira.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N7200000 and capital allowances of N2000000. What is the chargeable profit?
items.s: Chargeable profit = assessable profit - capital allowances = 7200000 - 2000000 = 5200000 naira.

items.q: A company made a profit of N5000000 for the year and has an unused loss of N1800000 brought forward from an earlier year. What profit is liable to tax?
items.s: Profit liable = profit for the year - loss brought forward = 5000000 - 1800000 = 3200000 naira.

items.q: A company has a profit of N8000000 and its total tax charge for the year was N1800000. What is its effective tax rate as a percentage?
items.s: Effective rate = tax charge/profit x 100 = 1800000/8000000 x 100 = 22.5 percent.

items.q: A company bought plant costing N3000000 and is granted an initial allowance of 50 percent. What is the initial allowance?
items.s: Initial allowance = cost x rate/100 = 3000000 x 50/100 = 1500000 naira.

items.q: A qualifying asset cost N2000000. Initial allowance of 50 percent was granted in the first year and the annual allowance is 20 percent of the written down value. What is the annual allowance in the second year?
items.s: Written down value = 2000000 - 1000000 = 1000000; annual allowance = 1000000 x 20/100 = 200000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N500000 is sold for N800000. What is the balancing charge?
items.s: Balancing charge = sale proceeds - written down value = 800000 - 500000 = 300000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N1500000 is sold for N800000. What is the balancing allowance?
items.s: Balancing allowance = written down value - sale proceeds = 1500000 - 800000 = 700000 naira.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N6000000 and capital allowances of N3200000. Capital allowances may be claimed only up to two thirds of the assessable profit. What amount of capital allowance is allowed against the profit?
items.s: Two thirds of the assessable profit is 4000000; the allowance claimed is limited to the lower of that and 3200000, which is 3200000 naira.

items.q: An asset bought for N7000000 was sold for N15000000, and N600000 was spent on fees to bring the sale about. Capital gains tax is charged at 10 percent. What is the tax payable?
An asset was sold for N10000000 and N250000 was paid out in fees connected with the sale. What are the net proceeds of disposal?
items.s: Net proceeds = gross proceeds - costs of disposal = 10000000 - 250000 = 9750000 naira.

items.q: A registered trader charged output tax of N3600000 for the month and suffered input tax of N900000. What value added tax is payable?
items.s: Tax payable = output tax - input tax = 3600000 - 900000 = 2700000 naira.

items.q: A price of N430000 includes value added tax at 7.5 percent. What amount of the price is the tax?
items.s: Tax = inclusive price x 7.5/107.5 = 430000 x 7.5/107.5 = 30000 naira.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines tax clearance certificate?
o: the document issued to a taxpayer to show that his affairs are settled for the stated years
the rate applied to the last slice of a person's income
the body that coordinates the tax authorities of the federation and the states
a trader whose turnover passes the stated limit and who must therefore register
items.s: tax clearance certificate: the document issued to a taxpayer to show that his affairs are settled for the stated years. The other options describe taxable person, joint tax board, marginal rate.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines balancing charge?
o: the willingness of the public to pay what they owe without being forced
what remains of the total profit of a company after capital allowances are taken off
the document given to the payee as proof that levy has been taken from his money
the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value
items.s: balancing charge: the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value. The other options describe tax morale, chargeable profit, credit note for tax withheld.

items.q: tax appeal tribunal may be defined as
o: the carrying of a dispute to a higher body after the authority has refused to amend
the formal statement sent to a taxpayer showing what the authority says he owes
the body that hears disputes on federal levies before any court is approached
the arranging of one's affairs within the law so that less levy falls due
items.s: tax appeal tribunal: the body that hears disputes on federal levies before any court is approached. The other options describe appeal, tax avoidance, notice of assessment.

items.q: Which of the following best describes total profit?
o: the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value
the assessable profit of a company together with any balancing charge
a levy whose rate rises as the amount charged grows
the excess of the levy charged on supplies over the levy suffered on purchases
items.s: total profit: the assessable profit of a company together with any balancing charge. The other options describe vat payable, balancing charge, progressive tax.

items.q: Which term is described by “the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy”?
o: regressive tax
tax
indirect tax
fiscal policy
items.s: fiscal policy is the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy.

items.q: Which of the following best describes state internal revenue service?
o: the funding of a company with so much borrowed money that little profit is left to charge
the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind
the authority that assesses and collects personal income tax within a state
a levy whose rate rises as the amount charged grows
items.s: state internal revenue service: the authority that assesses and collects personal income tax within a state. The other options describe thin capitalisation, emolument, progressive tax.

items.q: Which of the following best describes final tax?
o: a levy taken from the distribution of profit to shareholders before it is paid out
a levy taken at source that settles the liability on that income once and for all
the document issued to a taxpayer to show that his affairs are settled for the stated years
the arranging of one's affairs within the law so that less levy falls due
items.s: final tax: a levy taken at source that settles the liability on that income once and for all. The other options describe dividend withholding, tax avoidance, tax clearance certificate.

items.q: progressive tax may be defined as
o: the sale of only a portion of an interest in an asset
a step with no purpose beyond the reduction of levy, which the authority may disregard
a levy whose rate rises as the amount charged grows
the document a registered trader must issue showing the levy charged on a supply
items.s: progressive tax: a levy whose rate rises as the amount charged grows. The other options describe tax invoice, part disposal, artificial transaction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes unique taxpayer identification number?
o: the single reference by which one taxpayer is known to every tax office
a relief that frees a qualifying new industry from company tax for an initial period
the arranging of one's affairs within the law so that less levy falls due
a floor levy charged on a company whatever its profit, once it has traded for the stated period
items.s: unique taxpayer identification number: the single reference by which one taxpayer is known to every tax office. The other options describe minimum tax, pioneer status, tax avoidance.

items.q: Which term is described by “a step with no purpose beyond the reduction of levy, which the authority may disregard”?
o: tax avoidance
artificial transaction
transfer pricing
thin capitalisation
items.s: artificial transaction is a step with no purpose beyond the reduction of levy, which the authority may disregard.

items.q: All of the following belong to Tax administration in Nigeria EXCEPT
o: joint tax board
whistle blowing
federal inland revenue service
state internal revenue service
items.s: Every other option belongs to Tax administration in Nigeria. “whistle blowing” belongs to Tax avoidance, evasion and ethics, not Tax administration in Nigeria.

items.q: The statement “the postponement of a levy where the proceeds of a sale are laid out on a replacement asset” describes which of the following?
o: indexation relief
roll over relief
acquisition cost
incidental cost of disposal
items.s: roll over relief is the postponement of a levy where the proceeds of a sale are laid out on a replacement asset.

items.q: The statement “the levy a registered trader pays on what he buys for his business” describes which of the following?
o: input tax
zero rated supply
taxable person
vat payable
items.s: input tax is the levy a registered trader pays on what he buys for his business.

items.q: Which of the following best describes objection?
o: the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset
an examination of the records of a taxpayer to test whether the returns are right
the formal complaint of a taxpayer who disputes an assessment within the stated time
a levy taken at source that settles the liability on that income once and for all
items.s: objection: the formal complaint of a taxpayer who disputes an assessment within the stated time. The other options describe tax audit, annual allowance, final tax.

items.q: Which term is described by “a levy on the profit of a company used to support higher institutions”?
o: total profit
chargeable profit
tertiary education tax
minimum tax
items.s: tertiary education tax is a levy on the profit of a company used to support higher institutions.

items.q: The statement “the profit of a company after the adjustments allowed by the tax law but before capital allowances” describes which of the following?
o: assessable profit
capital allowance
loss relief
total profit
items.s: assessable profit is the profit of a company after the adjustments allowed by the tax law but before capital allowances.

items.q: Which of the following best describes pay as you earn?
o: the arrangement by which an employer deducts tax from wages and sends it to the authority
the levy a registered trader pays on what he buys for his business
a floor levy charged on a company whatever its profit, once it has traded for the stated period
property whose sale is left out of the charge on gains
items.s: pay as you earn: the arrangement by which an employer deducts tax from wages and sends it to the authority. The other options describe exempt asset, input tax, minimum tax.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines pay as you earn?
o: the document a registered trader must issue showing the levy charged on a supply
the arrangement by which an employer deducts tax from wages and sends it to the authority
the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
the reply of the authority where it declines to change an assessment it has raised
items.s: pay as you earn: the arrangement by which an employer deducts tax from wages and sends it to the authority. The other options describe written down value, tax invoice, notice of refusal to amend.

items.q: marginal rate may be defined as
o: a levy on the profit of a company used to support higher institutions
a levy taken from the payment made for building, supply or installation work
the carrying of a trading loss against the profit of another period
the rate applied to the last slice of a person's income
items.s: marginal rate: the rate applied to the last slice of a person's income. The other options describe contract withholding, tertiary education tax, loss relief.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines exempt supply?
o: the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
the document issued to a taxpayer to show that his affairs are settled for the stated years
a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered
a trader whose turnover passes the stated limit and who must therefore register
items.s: exempt supply: a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered. The other options describe tax clearance certificate, written down value, taxable person.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines fiscal policy?
o: the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy
the rate applied to the last slice of a person's income
the assessable profit of a company together with any balancing charge
the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies
items.s: fiscal policy: the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy. The other options describe total profit, output tax, marginal rate.

items.q: chargeable gain may be defined as
o: the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind
the increase in worth of an asset after the permitted deductions have been taken off
a levy whose burden is meant to stay on the person who pays it over
the sale of only a portion of an interest in an asset
items.s: chargeable gain: the increase in worth of an asset after the permitted deductions have been taken off. The other options describe emolument, direct tax, part disposal.

items.q: chargeable asset may be defined as
o: property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth
the body that hears disputes on federal levies before any court is approached
the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
the document issued to a taxpayer to show that his affairs are settled for the stated years
items.s: chargeable asset: property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth. The other options describe tax clearance certificate, written down value, tax appeal tribunal.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines indexation relief?
o: a trader whose turnover passes the stated limit and who must therefore register
the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset
an adjustment that strips out the effect of price inflation from a gain
the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
items.s: indexation relief: an adjustment that strips out the effect of price inflation from a gain. The other options describe taxable person, annual allowance, written down value.

items.q: The statement “property whose sale is left out of the charge on gains” describes which of the following?
o: incidental cost of disposal
chargeable gain
exempt asset
indexation relief
items.s: exempt asset is property whose sale is left out of the charge on gains.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines thin capitalisation.
o: the funding of a company with so much borrowed money that little profit is left to charge
the setting of the amounts charged between related companies for goods and services
the deduction allowed for the part of pay put into a approved retirement scheme
the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies
items.s: thin capitalisation: the funding of a company with so much borrowed money that little profit is left to charge. The other options describe output tax, transfer pricing, relief for pension contribution.

items.q: Which term is described by “a trader whose turnover passes the stated limit and who must therefore register”?
o: output tax
taxable person
zero rated supply
tax invoice
items.s: taxable person is a trader whose turnover passes the stated limit and who must therefore register.

items.q: balancing charge may be defined as
o: the form on which a taxpayer states his own income and works out his liability
the amount or thing on which a levy is worked out
the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value
items.s: balancing charge: the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value. The other options describe written down value, self assessment return, tax base.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines roll over relief.
o: the willingness of the public to pay what they owe without being forced
property whose sale is left out of the charge on gains
the authority that assesses and collects the levies of the federal government
the postponement of a levy where the proceeds of a sale are laid out on a replacement asset
items.s: roll over relief: the postponement of a levy where the proceeds of a sale are laid out on a replacement asset. The other options describe tax morale, exempt asset, federal inland revenue service.

items.q: The statement “a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government” describes which of the following?
o: indirect tax
fiscal policy
proportional tax
tax
items.s: indirect tax is a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government.

items.q: Which term is described by “the outlay on an asset of a kind that attracts a wear allowance”?
o: investment allowance
annual allowance
balancing allowance
qualifying capital expenditure
items.s: qualifying capital expenditure is the outlay on an asset of a kind that attracts a wear allowance.

items.q: tax evasion may be defined as
o: the unlawful escape from a levy by concealment or false statement
a trader whose turnover passes the stated limit and who must therefore register
the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies
the sale of only a portion of an interest in an asset
items.s: tax evasion: the unlawful escape from a levy by concealment or false statement. The other options describe output tax, part disposal, taxable person.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines annual allowance.
o: a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered
the profit of a company after the adjustments allowed by the tax law but before capital allowances
the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset
the single reference by which one taxpayer is known to every tax office
items.s: annual allowance: the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset. The other options describe assessable profit, unique taxpayer identification number, exempt supply.

items.q: Which of the following best describes chargeable gain?
o: a levy whose rate rises as the amount charged grows
the single reference by which one taxpayer is known to every tax office
the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
the increase in worth of an asset after the permitted deductions have been taken off
items.s: chargeable gain: the increase in worth of an asset after the permitted deductions have been taken off. The other options describe written down value, unique taxpayer identification number, progressive tax.

items.q: Which of the following best describes chargeable asset?
o: the carrying of a dispute to a higher body after the authority has refused to amend
the deduction granted in the first year an asset is put to use, before the yearly allowance
the funding of a company with so much borrowed money that little profit is left to charge
property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth
items.s: chargeable asset: property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth. The other options describe appeal, thin capitalisation, initial allowance.

items.q: emolument may be defined as
o: a compulsory levy imposed by a public authority on persons, goods or transactions to raise revenue
the carrying of a dispute to a higher body after the authority has refused to amend
the deduction granted in the first year an asset is put to use, before the yearly allowance
the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind
items.s: emolument: the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind. The other options describe appeal, tax, initial allowance.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines notice of refusal to amend?
o: a relief that frees a qualifying new industry from company tax for an initial period
the form on which a taxpayer states his own income and works out his liability
the reply of the authority where it declines to change an assessment it has raised
the formal statement sent to a taxpayer showing what the authority says he owes
items.s: notice of refusal to amend: the reply of the authority where it declines to change an assessment it has raised. The other options describe pioneer status, notice of assessment, self assessment return.

items.q: Which term is described by “the carrying of a dispute to a higher body after the authority has refused to amend”?
o: tax appeal tribunal
appeal
self assessment return
notice of refusal to amend
items.s: appeal is the carrying of a dispute to a higher body after the authority has refused to amend.

items.q: Which term is described by “a levy taken from the payment made to a practitioner for skilled services”?
o: professional fee withholding
final tax
withholding tax
deducting agent
items.s: professional fee withholding is a levy taken from the payment made to a practitioner for skilled services.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines emolument.
o: the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset
the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind
the outlay on an asset of a kind that attracts a wear allowance
the funding of a company with so much borrowed money that little profit is left to charge
items.s: emolument: the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind. The other options describe qualifying capital expenditure, thin capitalisation, annual allowance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines credit note for tax withheld.
o: an adjustment that strips out the effect of price inflation from a gain
the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind
the document given to the payee as proof that levy has been taken from his money
the excess of the levy charged on supplies over the levy suffered on purchases

a levy taken from the payment made to a practitioner for skilled services
the party who is required by law to take the levy out of a payment before releasing it
the levy a registered trader pays on what he buys for his business

chargeable asset
chargeable gain

the levy a registered trader pays on what he buys for his business

items.q: Which term is described by “the form on which a taxpayer states his own income and works out his liability”?

tax appeal tribunal
self assessment return
objection

tertiary education tax
chargeable profit
minimum tax

a charge raised by the authority on its own estimate where the taxpayer fails to file
a levy whose rate rises as the amount charged grows
the body that coordinates the tax authorities of the federation and the states

joint tax board
state internal revenue service
self assessment

the formal statement sent to a taxpayer showing what the authority says he owes
the increase in worth of an asset after the permitted deductions have been taken off

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines unique taxpayer identification number.
o: the willingness of the public to pay what they owe without being forced
a levy taken at source that settles the liability on that income once and for all
the single reference by which one taxpayer is known to every tax office
the outlay on an asset of a kind that attracts a wear allowance

vat payable
zero rated supply
input tax

a fresh charge raised where it is later found that too little was assessed
the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value
the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset

federal inland revenue service
tax clearance certificate
tax audit

the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies
what remains of the total profit of a company after capital allowances are taken off
the assessable profit of a company together with any balancing charge

the assessable profit of a company together with any balancing charge
the levy a registered trader pays on what he buys for his business
the total levy divided by the whole income on which it was charged

a charge raised by the authority on its own estimate where the taxpayer fails to file

a system in which the taxpayer works out his own liability and files it
the reporting of another person's hiding of income to the authority

the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value
the reply of the authority where it declines to change an assessment it has raised
property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth

the shortfall allowed when an asset is sold for less than its written down value
the sale of only a portion of an interest in an asset
the authority that assesses and collects the levies of the federal government

items.q: indirect tax may be defined as

a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government
the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies
a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered

items.q: Which term is described by “the rate applied to the last slice of a person's income”?

marginal rate
average rate
gross income

a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered

the document given to the payee as proof that levy has been taken from his money

a system in which the taxpayer works out his own liability and files it
the body that coordinates the tax authorities of the federation and the states
a levy taken from the payment made for the use of property

a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered
property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth
the forward arranging of transactions so that the levy payable is lawfully reduced

o: roll over relief
part disposal
chargeable gain
acquisition cost

items.q: An individual has taxable income of N1500000 and pays tax at 15 percent. What is the income left after tax?
An employee earns basic salary of N3000000 a year and contributes 10 percent of it to a pension scheme. What amount is allowed as relief for the contribution?
items.s: Relief = basic salary x rate/100 = 3000000 x 10/100 = 300000 naira.

items.q: A company bought plant costing N3000000 and is granted an initial allowance of 25 percent. What is the initial allowance?
items.s: Initial allowance = cost x rate/100 = 3000000 x 25/100 = 750000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N500000 is sold for N1200000. What is the balancing charge?
items.s: Balancing charge = sale proceeds - written down value = 1200000 - 500000 = 700000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N1200000 is sold for N800000. What is the balancing allowance?
items.s: Balancing allowance = written down value - sale proceeds = 1200000 - 800000 = 400000 naira.

items.q: An asset bought for N5000000 was sold for N12000000, and N600000 was spent on fees to bring the sale about. Capital gains tax is charged at 10 percent. What is the tax payable?
An asset was sold for N14000000 and N750000 was paid out in fees connected with the sale. What are the net proceeds of disposal?
items.s: Net proceeds = gross proceeds - costs of disposal = 14000000 - 750000 = 13250000 naira.

items.q: A company pays a supplier N3000000 for a contract and must withhold tax at 5 percent. How much tax is withheld?
items.s: Tax withheld = gross payment x rate/100 = 3000000 x 5/100 = 150000 naira.

items.q: A payment of N1200000 is subject to withholding tax at 10 percent. What amount reaches the payee?
A taxpayer files his return late and the law imposes a penalty equal to 10 percent of the tax due. The tax due is N2000000. What is the penalty?
items.s: Penalty = tax due x 10/100 = 2000000 x 10/100 = 200000 naira.

items.q: An employee earns gross income of N4800000 in a year. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200000 or 1 percent of gross income, plus 20 percent of gross income. What is the taxable income?
items.s: Relief = higher of N200000 and 1 percent of 4800000 = N200000; allowance = 200000 + 20 percent of 4800000 = 1160000; taxable income = 4800000 - 1160000 = 3640000 naira.

items.q: A taxpayer has gross income of N3600000. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200000 or 1 percent of gross income, plus 20 percent of gross income. What is the allowance?
items.s: The fixed part is the higher of N200000 and N36000, and the proportional part is 20 percent of 3600000 = N720000, so the allowance is 200000 + 720000 = 920000 naira.

items.q: Taxable income is N700000. The first N400000 is charged at 15 percent and the balance at 24 percent. What is the total tax?
An individual with taxable income of N2400000 paid tax of N420000. What is the average rate of tax as a percentage?
items.s: Average rate = total tax/taxable income x 100 = 420000/2400000 x 100 = 17.5 percent.

items.q: Gross income for the year is N2000000 and the total reliefs allowed are N600000. What is the taxable income?
items.s: Taxable income = gross income - reliefs = 2000000 - 600000 = 1400000 naira.

items.q: A company made a profit of N6500000 for the year and has an unused loss of N1800000 brought forward from an earlier year. What profit is liable to tax?
items.s: Profit liable = profit for the year - loss brought forward = 6500000 - 1800000 = 4700000 naira.

items.q: A company has assessable profit of N4000000 and pays tertiary education tax at 2.5 percent. What is the charge?
items.s: Education tax = assessable profit x 2.5/100 = 4000000 x 2.5/100 = 100000 naira.

items.q: A company has a profit of N6000000 and its total tax charge for the year was N2400000. What is its effective tax rate as a percentage?
items.s: Effective rate = tax charge/profit x 100 = 2400000/6000000 x 100 = 40 percent.

items.q: A qualifying asset cost N3000000. Initial allowance of 25 percent was granted in the first year and the annual allowance is 12 percent of the written down value. What is the annual allowance in the second year?
items.s: Written down value = 3000000 - 750000 = 2250000; annual allowance = 2250000 x 12/100 = 270000 naira.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N4000000 and capital allowances of N5200000. Capital allowances may be claimed only up to two thirds of the assessable profit. What amount of capital allowance is allowed against the profit?
items.s: Two thirds of the assessable profit is 2666666; the allowance claimed is limited to the lower of that and 5200000, which is 4000000 naira.

items.q: A chargeable asset was acquired for N5500000 and later sold for N9000000. Incidental costs of N450000 were incurred on the sale. What is the chargeable gain?
items.s: Chargeable gain = proceeds - acquisition cost - incidental costs = 9000000 - 5500000 - 450000 = 3050000 naira.

items.q: A price of N1290000 includes value added tax at 7.5 percent. What amount of the price is the tax?
items.s: Tax = inclusive price x 7.5/107.5 = 1290000 x 7.5/107.5 = 90000 naira.

items.q: A trader made taxable supplies of N14000000 in the first half of the year and N12000000 in the second half. Registration is required once taxable turnover for the year reaches N25000000. What is the taxable turnover for the year that is tested against that limit?
items.s: Turnover for the year = 14000000 + 12000000 = 26000000 naira, which is the figure compared with the N25000000 limit.

items.q: A company declares a dividend of N2400000 to its shareholders and withholds tax at 10 percent. What tax is withheld?
items.s: Tax withheld = dividend x 10/100 = 2400000 x 10/100 = 240000 naira.

items.q: A dividend of N2500000 is paid to a shareholder and tax of 10 percent is withheld as a final tax. What amount does the shareholder receive?
items.s: Tax withheld = 2500000 x 10/100 = 250000; amount received = 2500000 - 250000 = 2250000 naira.

items.q: Tax of N4800000 is paid 6 months late and interest is charged at 2 percent for each month of delay. What interest is payable?
items.s: Interest = tax x rate/100 x months = 4800000 x 2/100 x 6 = 576000 naira.

items.q: An assessment of N3200000 has been raised and the taxpayer has already paid N2000000 against it. What balance is still outstanding?
items.s: Balance = assessment - amount paid = 3200000 - 2000000 = 1200000 naira.

items.q: A trader made sales of N4000000 during the month and collected value added tax of N750000. What is the tax as a percentage of sales?
items.s: Tax as a percentage of sales = 750000/4000000 x 100 = 18.75 percent.

items.q: The tax declared by a taxpayer was N3000000 but a tax audit established that N4000000 was properly due. What is the tax shortfall?
items.s: Shortfall = correct liability - amount declared = 4000000 - 3000000 = 1000000 naira.

items.q: An individual has taxable income of N2000000 and falls into the top band, which is charged at 15 percent. What is the tax on the whole income at that rate?
items.s: Tax = taxable income x rate/100 = 2000000 x 15/100 = 300000 naira.

items.q: An individual has taxable income of N3200000 and pays tax at 15 percent. What is the income left after tax?
An employee earns basic salary of N4200000 a year and contributes 8 percent of it to a pension scheme. What amount is allowed as relief for the contribution?
items.s: Relief = basic salary x rate/100 = 4200000 x 8/100 = 336000 naira.

items.q: A company has total profit of N5000000 and pays company income tax at 20 percent. What is the tax charge?
items.s: Tax charge = total profit x rate/100 = 5000000 x 20/100 = 1000000 naira.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N5600000 and capital allowances of N1600000. What is the chargeable profit?
items.s: Chargeable profit = assessable profit - capital allowances = 5600000 - 1600000 = 4000000 naira.

items.q: A company bought plant costing N4500000 and is granted an initial allowance of 50 percent. What is the initial allowance?
items.s: Initial allowance = cost x rate/100 = 4500000 x 50/100 = 2250000 naira.

items.q: An asset bought for N7000000 was sold for N12000000, and N600000 was spent on fees to bring the sale about. Capital gains tax is charged at 10 percent. What is the tax payable?
An asset was sold for N14000000 and N250000 was paid out in fees connected with the sale. What are the net proceeds of disposal?
items.s: Net proceeds = gross proceeds - costs of disposal = 14000000 - 250000 = 13750000 naira.

items.q: A registered trader charged output tax of N1800000 for the month and suffered input tax of N1500000. What value added tax is payable?
items.s: Tax payable = output tax - input tax = 1800000 - 1500000 = 300000 naira.

items.q: A company pays a supplier N5000000 for a contract and must withhold tax at 5 percent. How much tax is withheld?
items.s: Tax withheld = gross payment x rate/100 = 5000000 x 5/100 = 250000 naira.

items.q: A payment of N3600000 is subject to withholding tax at 10 percent. What amount reaches the payee?
A company was first assessed on N1400000 and a later audit showed the correct figure to be N3200000. What is the additional assessment?
items.s: Additional assessment = correct figure - original assessment = 3200000 - 1400000 = 1800000 naira.

items.q: An employee earns gross income of N2400000 in a year. The consolidated relief allowance is the higher of N200000 or 1 percent of gross income, plus 20 percent of gross income. What is the taxable income?
items.s: Relief = higher of N200000 and 1 percent of 2400000 = N200000; allowance = 200000 + 20 percent of 2400000 = 680000; taxable income = 2400000 - 680000 = 1720000 naira.

items.q: Taxable income is N900000. The first N500000 is charged at 11 percent and the balance at 19 percent. What is the total tax?
An individual with taxable income of N2400000 paid tax of N240000. What is the average rate of tax as a percentage?
items.s: Average rate = total tax/taxable income x 100 = 240000/2400000 x 100 = 10 percent.

items.q: The assessable profit of a company is N4200000 and a balancing charge of N200000 arises on the disposal of an asset. What is the total profit?
items.s: Total profit = assessable profit + balancing charge = 4200000 + 200000 = 4400000 naira.

items.q: A company has assessable profit of N16000000 and pays tertiary education tax at 2.5 percent. What is the charge?
items.s: Education tax = assessable profit x 2.5/100 = 16000000 x 2.5/100 = 400000 naira.

items.q: A company has a profit of N6000000 and its total tax charge for the year was N1800000. What is its effective tax rate as a percentage?
items.s: Effective rate = tax charge/profit x 100 = 1800000/6000000 x 100 = 30 percent.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N6000000 and capital allowances of N5200000. Capital allowances may be claimed only up to two thirds of the assessable profit. What amount of capital allowance is allowed against the profit?
items.s: Two thirds of the assessable profit is 4000000; the allowance claimed is limited to the lower of that and 5200000, which is 5200000 naira.

items.q: A chargeable gain of N5000000 arises and capital gains tax is charged at 10 percent. What is the tax payable?
A taxable supply is made for N1200000 before tax and value added tax is charged at 7.5 percent. What tax is added?
A taxable supply was invoiced at N540000 inclusive of value added tax at 7.5 percent. What is the price before tax?
items.s: Price before tax = inclusive amount x 100/107.5 = 540000 x 100/107.5 = 502325 naira.

items.q: A trader made taxable supplies of N18000000 in the first half of the year and N10000000 in the second half. Registration is required once taxable turnover for the year reaches N25000000. What is the taxable turnover for the year that is tested against that limit?
items.s: Turnover for the year = 18000000 + 10000000 = 28000000 naira, which is the figure compared with the N25000000 limit.

items.q: A company pays N2000000 for professional services, taxed at 10 percent, and N1200000 as rent, taxed at 5 percent. What total withholding tax must it remit?
Tax of N4800000 is paid 3 months late and interest is charged at 2 percent for each month of delay. What interest is payable?
items.s: Interest = tax x rate/100 x months = 4800000 x 2/100 x 3 = 288000 naira.

items.q: An individual has taxable income of N2500000 and falls into the top band, which is charged at 15 percent. What is the tax on the whole income at that rate?
items.s: Tax = taxable income x rate/100 = 2500000 x 15/100 = 375000 naira.

items.q: An employee earns basic salary of N4200000 a year and contributes 7 percent of it to a pension scheme. What amount is allowed as relief for the contribution?
items.s: Relief = basic salary x rate/100 = 4200000 x 7/100 = 294000 naira.

items.q: A company has total profit of N9000000 and pays company income tax at 20 percent. What is the tax charge?
items.s: Tax charge = total profit x rate/100 = 9000000 x 20/100 = 1800000 naira.

items.q: A company has an assessable profit of N5600000 and capital allowances of N1200000. What is the chargeable profit?
items.s: Chargeable profit = assessable profit - capital allowances = 5600000 - 1200000 = 4400000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N700000 is sold for N800000. What is the balancing charge?
items.s: Balancing charge = sale proceeds - written down value = 800000 - 700000 = 100000 naira.

items.q: An asset with a written down value of N1500000 is sold for N600000. What is the balancing allowance?
items.s: Balancing allowance = written down value - sale proceeds = 1500000 - 600000 = 900000 naira.

a levy taken at source from a payment and handed to the authority by the payer

the willingness of the public to pay what they owe without being forced

deducting agent
credit note for tax withheld
final tax

o: artificial transaction
transfer pricing
tax morale
thin capitalisation
items.s: tax morale is the willingness of the public to pay what they owe without being forced.

the single reference by which one taxpayer is known to every tax office
the body that coordinates the tax authorities of the federation and the states

the assessable profit of a company together with any balancing charge

the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies

what is left of a person's income after the permitted deductions have been taken off
the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind

capital allowance
total profit
minimum tax

the whole of what a person receives from every source before any deduction is made

dividend withholding
final tax
contract withholding

the setting of the amounts charged between related companies for goods and services
the willingness of the public to pay what they owe without being forced

the profit of a company after the adjustments allowed by the tax law but before capital allowances
the assessable profit of a company together with any balancing charge
a relief that frees a qualifying new industry from company tax for an initial period
items.s: pioneer status: a relief that frees a qualifying new industry from company tax for an initial period. The other options describe total profit, minimum tax, assessable profit.

items.q: “the party who is required by law to take the levy out of a payment before releasing it” is the definition of
o: credit note for tax withheld
withholding tax
deducting agent
dividend withholding
items.s: deducting agent is the party who is required by law to take the levy out of a payment before releasing it.

items.q: The correct meaning of marginal rate is
o: what is left of a person's income after the permitted deductions have been taken off
a deduction granted to an individual for his own upkeep and that of his dependants
the rate applied to the last slice of a person's income
the whole of the reward a person gets from an employment, whether in money or in kind
items.s: marginal rate: the rate applied to the last slice of a person's income. The other options describe emolument, taxable income, personal allowance.

items.q: In this course, tax audit refers to
o: the body that coordinates the tax authorities of the federation and the states
the arrangement by which an employer deducts tax from wages and sends it to the authority
a system in which the taxpayer works out his own liability and files it
an examination of the records of a taxpayer to test whether the returns are right
items.s: tax audit: an examination of the records of a taxpayer to test whether the returns are right. The other options describe joint tax board, self assessment, pay as you earn.

items.q: The correct meaning of zero rated supply is
o: a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered
the levy a registered trader pays on what he buys for his business
the rule that makes the buyer account for the levy on a supply obtained from outside the country
a supply charged at nothing but still treated as taxable so that the levy on purchases may be recovered
items.s: zero rated supply: a supply charged at nothing but still treated as taxable so that the levy on purchases may be recovered. The other options describe input tax, exempt supply, reverse charge.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines annual allowance?
o: the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
the deduction granted in the first year an asset is put to use, before the yearly allowance
the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset
the group of like assets whose allowances are worked out together
items.s: annual allowance: the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset. The other options describe written down value, pool, initial allowance.

items.q: “the deduction granted in the first year an asset is put to use, before the yearly allowance” is the definition of
o: balancing charge
qualifying capital expenditure
initial allowance
annual allowance
items.s: initial allowance is the deduction granted in the first year an asset is put to use, before the yearly allowance.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies”
o: output tax
taxable person
exempt supply
vat payable
items.s: output tax is the levy a registered trader adds to the price of what he supplies.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains indexation relief.
o: the sale of only a portion of an interest in an asset
what the seller gave to obtain the asset in the first place
an adjustment that strips out the effect of price inflation from a gain
property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth
items.s: indexation relief: an adjustment that strips out the effect of price inflation from a gain. The other options describe part disposal, acquisition cost, chargeable asset.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines dividend withholding?
o: a levy taken from the distribution of profit to shareholders before it is paid out
a levy taken at source that settles the liability on that income once and for all
a levy taken from the payment made to a practitioner for skilled services
a levy taken from the payment made for the use of property
items.s: dividend withholding: a levy taken from the distribution of profit to shareholders before it is paid out. The other options describe final tax, rent withholding, professional fee withholding.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains indirect tax.
o: a levy that takes a larger share of a small income than of a large one
a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government
a levy that applies one single rate whatever the size of the amount charged
the amount or thing on which a levy is worked out
items.s: indirect tax: a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government. The other options describe regressive tax, tax base, proportional tax.

items.q: “an extra deduction granted on plant bought for use in a rural area” is the definition of
o: balancing charge
investment allowance
qualifying capital expenditure
annual allowance
items.s: investment allowance is an extra deduction granted on plant bought for use in a rural area.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains pool.
o: the cost of an asset less the allowances already granted on it
an extra deduction granted on plant bought for use in a rural area
the outlay on an asset of a kind that attracts a wear allowance
the group of like assets whose allowances are worked out together
items.s: pool: the group of like assets whose allowances are worked out together. The other options describe qualifying capital expenditure, written down value, investment allowance.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government”
o: tax base
fiscal policy
regressive tax
indirect tax
items.s: indirect tax is a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains fiscal policy.
o: a levy that applies one single rate whatever the size of the amount charged
the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy
a levy that takes a larger share of a small income than of a large one
a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government
items.s: fiscal policy: the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy. The other options describe proportional tax, regressive tax, indirect tax.

items.q: The correct meaning of incidental cost of disposal is
o: what the seller gave to obtain the asset in the first place
property of a kind whose sale gives rise to a levy on the increase in its worth
the outlay needed to bring a sale about, such as fees and advertising
the postponement of a levy where the proceeds of a sale are laid out on a replacement asset
items.s: incidental cost of disposal: the outlay needed to bring a sale about, such as fees and advertising. The other options describe roll over relief, acquisition cost, chargeable asset.

items.q: “the increase in worth of an asset after the permitted deductions have been taken off” is the definition of
o: chargeable gain
acquisition cost
indexation relief
exempt asset
items.s: chargeable gain is the increase in worth of an asset after the permitted deductions have been taken off.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a levy that applies one single rate whatever the size of the amount charged”
o: regressive tax
proportional tax
fiscal policy
tax
items.s: proportional tax is a levy that applies one single rate whatever the size of the amount charged.

items.q: The correct meaning of whistle blowing is
o: the reporting of another person's hiding of income to the authority
a step with no purpose beyond the reduction of levy, which the authority may disregard
the setting of the amounts charged between related companies for goods and services
the arranging of one's affairs within the law so that less levy falls due
items.s: whistle blowing: the reporting of another person's hiding of income to the authority. The other options describe artificial transaction, tax avoidance, transfer pricing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines direct tax?
o: a levy whose burden is meant to stay on the person who pays it over
a levy that takes a larger share of a small income than of a large one
a levy collected by a trader from the buyer and passed on to the government
the amount or thing on which a levy is worked out
items.s: direct tax: a levy whose burden is meant to stay on the person who pays it over. The other options describe tax base, indirect tax, regressive tax.

items.q: In this course, fiscal policy refers to
o: a levy that takes a larger share of a small income than of a large one
a levy that applies one single rate whatever the size of the amount charged
the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy
the amount or thing on which a levy is worked out
items.s: fiscal policy: the use of public revenue and spending to steady the economy. The other options describe proportional tax, regressive tax, tax base.

items.q: In this course, appeal refers to
o: the reply of the authority where it declines to change an assessment it has raised
the carrying of a dispute to a higher body after the authority has refused to amend
a charge raised by the authority on its own estimate where the taxpayer fails to file
the formal complaint of a taxpayer who disputes an assessment within the stated time
items.s: appeal: the carrying of a dispute to a higher body after the authority has refused to amend. The other options describe objection, best of judgement assessment, notice of refusal to amend.

items.q: The correct meaning of exempt supply is
o: a supply charged at nothing but still treated as taxable so that the levy on purchases may be recovered
the rule that makes the buyer account for the levy on a supply obtained from outside the country
a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered
the excess of the levy charged on supplies over the levy suffered on purchases
items.s: exempt supply: a supply outside the charge altogether, so that the levy on related purchases may not be recovered. The other options describe reverse charge, vat payable, zero rated supply.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines qualifying capital expenditure?
o: the deduction granted in each year after the first for the wear of the asset
the amount brought into charge when an asset is sold for more than its written down value
the outlay on an asset of a kind that attracts a wear allowance
the shortfall allowed when an asset is sold for less than its written down value
items.s: qualifying capital expenditure: the outlay on an asset of a kind that attracts a wear allowance. The other options describe balancing charge, balancing allowance, annual allowance.
